input.quote: HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.
input.rationale: Section 1.4 is the only grant running in our favour (access to and the right to use HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools). It runs to the Company alone: it is silent on affiliates, with no mechanism to add them, which fails even the fallback position that affiliates are covered on written notice. We therefore propose the complete fallback — affiliate coverage on written notice plus transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction — as a single appended sentence, leaving the bandwidth, burst-capacity and administration-tool obligations untouched. Preferred-only limbs (contractors, perpetual/irrevocable paid-up rights) are not pursued here because this Section grants term-based hosting access rather than a paid-up licence. The outbound Marks licence in Section 6.1 runs in our favour as licensor and is not flagged.

ops.text: The access and use rights granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 extend to any affiliate of the Company covered by written notice to HDI, and may be transferred to a successor to the Company's business in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates on written notice to HDI and confirmed they transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction, which is our fallback licence-scope position; the grant as drafted covers only the Company alone.
proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to Company affiliates on written notice and make them transferable to an M&A successor.

mappings.element: Licence transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
